title: Antelope-horn trumpet
summary: The Kajji side-blown trumpet is made from a curved antelope horn with a mouth hole near the tip and a hollow gourd fixed to the open end to lengthen it. The player blows across the hole, using close intervals, and solo players draw violin-like tones from it.
howToPlay: Four close notes are lit along the horn, the higher ones nearer the mouth hole.
A band of breath runs from the mouth hole to the note you strike, and rings of sound leave the gourd.
Long notes swell slowly: strike close to the beat and let them ring.
rules: A call is a line of long notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The horn is played together with a large and a small drum in the village band.
credits: Tradition: the Kajji horn; phrases written for this game
